title: The two-primary Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula in Selmer corank at most one
main_claim: For every elliptic curve E/Q with 2^infinity-Selmer corank s_2(E) <= 1: rank E(Q) = ord_{s=1} L(E,s) = s_2(E), Sha(E/Q) is finite, and v_2 of the BSD quotient Q_E equals v_2(#Sha). No restriction on E[2] or on the reduction type at 2. Corollaries: the same holds if s_p(E) <= 1 for any p (via a companion paper), and it holds for a density-one set of quadratic twists, with rank 0 and rank 1 each at density 1/2.
coverage: This was a partial audit of a 9,130-line paper. Read in full: the introduction (sec 1), the classical inputs (sec 2), the conclusion (sec 15), the positive completion (sec 7), and the first half of sec 5 (the integral positive determinant, the fixed-factor lemma and residual concentration). From sec 13 (real S3 anchor) I read the Pfaffian lemmas, and from sec 11 (CM) the opening and the residual-lift lemma. Checked and found OK: (a) The top-level deduction. The anchor gives an(E^h)+an(E^{hk}) = 1 and X(E^h)+X(E^{hk}) = 0. Nonnegativity then forces both X to be 0. Exactly one of h and hk is a positive fundamental discriminant prime to 2N, which feeds the positive transfer. CM curves go separately through Prop cm. (b) Corollary (G) agrees with the Gross-Zagier BSD reformulation: index^2 / (c_E^2 * prod c_l^2 * #Sha(E/K)), with u = 1 and the torsion handled through the full index. (c) Two-primary parity lemma, including that dim Sel_2 - dim E(Q)[2] - s_2 is even. (d) The weighted Pfaffian and adjugate identities (Pf(D B D) = det(D) Pf(B), and D #A D = Q #B, checked algebraically). The alternating-presentation construction needs no division by 2. (e) D_q/P_q has central value 1 at good and multiplicative primes, and the fixed factors are nonzero mod 2 because the cyclotomic exponents of q, c, d are nonzero. (f) The self-cup primitive lemma: Sha^2(Q_2(1)) = 0 by class field theory, plus local isotropy. (g) The length count in the rank-one central-value lemma. (h) In the CM residual-lift lemma, the required twist is anticyclotomic of odd order. Not verified line by line: the Siegel/Kato full-level reciprocity and integrality at 2 (sec 4), the tame spectral-height comparison (sec 6), the split measures (secs 8-9), and the reducible, imaginary and cyclic anchors (secs 10, 12, 14). Most of the CM determinant work in sec 11 was also not checked. These parts are written in a highly compressed way ('ultrafilter limits', 'Artin matrix limits', 'bounded-derived-length' Chebotarev arguments), so a referee would need far more time to confirm them. I found no specific step that fails, but this coverage does not certify those sections.
sibling_notes: The family-002 board was empty when I started. I checked the companions directly for circularity. The Goldfeld-density companion cites this paper only in its introduction, for the density corollary. It does not use it in the proof of its Theorem 1.2, which this paper's density corollary relies on. The all-prime Selmer converse companion does not cite this paper. So there is no circular dependence. The only cross-paper slip is a citation mismatch: the companion calls the twist corollary 'Corollary 16.1', but here it sits in section 15. That is not mathematical. I posted my summary to the board.
